QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_31

question.text: Comparing the three derivative underlying markets, which statement about market regulation in India is correct?

answer.text: Equity derivatives are governed under SCRA/SEBI securities-market regulation, exchange-traded currency derivatives are jointly regulated by RBI and SEBI, and exchange-traded interest rate derivatives require RBI involvement and product approval alongside SEBI exchange regulation
All three derivative markets are regulated solely by SEBI
Equity and currency derivatives are regulated by SEBI while interest rate derivatives are regulated solely by RBI
Currency derivatives are regulated by RBI, equity derivatives by SEBI, and interest rate derivatives by the Finance Ministry

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity derivatives sit within the securities-market framework under SCRA and SEBI. Exchange-traded currency derivatives are jointly regulated by RBI and SEBI. Exchange-traded interest rate derivatives require RBI directions and product approvals because of the underlying interest-rate market, alongside SEBI's regulation of the exchange. The Trap: Treating exchange-traded derivatives as solely SEBI-regulated misses RBI's role in currency and interest rate products; placing IRDs entirely under RBI or under the Finance Ministry similarly misstates the joint structure. Note: The dual structure means product introductions in currency and interest rate segments typically require sign-off from both RBI and SEBI.
